## Natural history notes

A small pyralid moth characterized by narrow brown to grayish-brown wings with subtle pale markings and a folded resting posture typical of many webworm moths. In Florida, it is associated with pawpaws in the genus Asimina, including scrub, pine flatwoods, hammocks, forest edges, and sandy open woodlands where native pawpaw species grow. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on pawpaw leaves, tying or webbing leaves together into shelters and sometimes defoliating shoots; this feeding can stimulate new pawpaw growth that may also be used by zebra swallowtail caterpillars.
